observations: Chase 1 holds 17 crates + 2 C and no explosives; the free section holds 23 crates incl. all 3 TNT, the first Nitro, the only Aku, the ! group and the bonus; chase 2 holds 4 crates but 3 Nitros.
Chase crates sit at landings (after the log, at the foot of drops) and work as snags; the guide says spin through or ignore.
The chaser smashes and credits missed crates, so the all-box goal never forces a risky stop in a chase; the Aku must be broken by Crash, so it sits in the free section.
The start trio triggers the chase: the player stops to smash it and the dinosaur bursts out behind him.
Checkpoints mark mode changes: C1 breather in chase 1, C19 ends it, C28 after the explosives, C58 at the drop that starts chase 2.
Explosive teaching order: TNT single, TNT 2-stack, Nitro inside a normal group, Nitro lane line in a chase, green ! at the exit.
Time Trial re-uses three ordinary crate positions as Aku crates so a clean run is invincible for the grass/magma strip.
The red-gem secret course has no crates; the all-box total is independent of it.
Bonus centrepiece: the tool (arrow) is on top of the stack you must dismantle.
badgeConvention: ttBadges: red 1 / blue 2 / green 3 = time-stop crate seconds in time trial; A = crate that is an Aku crate in time trial. Drawn icon = normal-mode type. Key 'wood?' = a counted crate whose type cannot be read (gutter blur or hidden behind a badge)
countingRule: F3 cumulative counts include the checkpoint crate; 'NN (MM)' = without (with) Nitro. After the green ! all 4 Nitro count. Steel !, green !, steel platform and steel C-blocks are not boxes: listed under 'uncounted' (count 0). The bonus (14) is inside the C58 count.

geometryObservations: **Two speeds, two geometries.** The chases run down narrow ≈3–5 u corridors toward the camera with hazards at the edges; the free section uses wider flat floors for explosives (the TNT ladder) and a switch puzzle over the lava river.

**Chase 1 never closes the lane except with a log.** Lava patches and geysers alternate sides (P3 s50) and leave half the path open; the only full-width obstacles are a fallen log and step-downs, both answered by one short move.

**Drops commit the player and carry crates on the landing.** Every step-down (S1, S2, the C58 drop) has crates at its foot; TT 05 and 23: drop without jumping, from the centre, and do not snag. The landing snag is the chase’s typical crate placement.

**The pursuer makes crate snags fair.** Missed crates are smashed and credited by the triceratops (F3 tip 2), so crates can stand on the chase line as obstacles, and the all-box goal never forces a stop inside a chase.

**Clinging grass is taught in the order slow → deadly.** Small patches at the S1 step, carpets in the free strip (harmless at walking pace), a field in chase 2 with a stepping crate and a safe lane, the middle of the final choke, and the whole gem course.
**The free section rehearses the chase vocabulary at walking pace.** Strip 2 holds lava patches, logs, grass and ambushers and no crates, so the obstacle language is learned where failure is cheap.

**Full-width lava appears late.** Bands are first met at walking pace in the lava-river area, then in chase 2 (a ≈1 u band, a ≈2–3 u pool), then as pools needing the super double jump on the secret course.

**Enemies match the pace.** Pterodactyls (flank ambushers that swoop across the lane) live in the chases, the wave assistants (puddle ambushers) only in the free section, and the invincible triceratops supplies the pressure.
**Mode changes are geometry changes.** Chase 1 ends at the C19 curve where the route turns back into the screen; chase 2 starts at a one-way step-down above C58. Both are checkpoints.

**The finale narrows the lane.** A big lava patch and three Nitros leave one third of the path, then a lava | grass | lava choke offers two wrong answers and one right one, followed by the green ! — the stage’s count check placed at its tightest point.
**The bonus is safe geometry around an order puzzle.** Steps of ≈0.5 u, gaps under 1 u and a floating steel shelf reachable only by the arrow once the stack below it is dismantled.
**The secret course is harder geometry, not more crates:** a narrower strip, more birds, water currents as speed boosts, steel checkpoints and pools that assume the super double jump from stage 12.

**Time-trial masks are placed as geometry keys.** Three crates become Aku crates so that invincibility covers exactly the grass and magma stretch after the TNT ladder (TT 13–20: landing in magma is fine while masked).
geometryTransfer: **Pursuer runs with a walking break.** Use the level-data `boulderChase` with two runs separated by `shelters`: run 1 down a 3.5–6 m (3–5 u) corridor with hazards on alternating edges and one full-width hurdle; a free section with the explosives and the switch puzzle; run 2 starting with a one-way 1.2–2.3 m drop. Missed crates should be credited when the pursuer breaks them, or kept off the chase line.

**Landing snags at drops.** Put one crate on the landing of each 1.2–2.3 m step-down, slightly off-centre: on foot it teaches "drop, don’t jump"; on the board a plow at ≥ 13 m/s costs ≈ 20 % speed, so a chase line should hold at most two in a row.

**Slow patch with an island and a safe lane.** In a chase, cover two thirds of the lane with slow ground, stand a crate in it as an island (top 1.15 m: inside a full ollie’s 1.78 m apex and a plain jump on foot), and leave a 1.2–1.5 m clean lane along one wall, visible early.

**Perched flank ambusher.** A `floater` (hovers 1.65 m, swoops every 2.6 s within 12 m along and 6 m across) on a perch at the corridor edge plays the pterodactyl; place them on alternating edges, never on the landing of a drop.

**Final squeeze before the goal.** Lava `pit`s on both edges with a slow patch between them, and a Nitro line along one edge after a wide lava patch, 2–3 s before the `nitrobang` and the gate: the lane narrows to ≈1.2 m at chase speed, and the count check sits at the tightest point.

**Arrow-on-tower bonus geometry.** Keep the bonus footing trivial (0.5 m steps, gaps ≤ 1 m) and put the difficulty in the order. Build the reward shelf from steel crates (crate tops cannot be ledge-grabbed, unlike platforms) with its top 5–5.8 m above the floor, inside the arrow-gate window (4.7–6.6 m, bible XV.2): an arrow resting on one crate (lid 2.30 m) launches ≈ 3.77 m above its lid (≈ 6.1 m), while the arrow on top of a 5-stack (lid 5.76 m) is above the floor double jump (4.59 m) until the stack below it is reduced.
